title: Maryam bint Imran
subtitle: The only woman named in the Qur'an — chosen above the women of the worlds
sources: Qur'an 19 (Surah Maryam, entire)
Qur'an 3:42-51 — the annunciation
Qur'an 66:12 — 'and she believed in the words of her Lord'
Qur'an 21:91 — the spirit blown into her, her and her son a sign

chapters.heading: The Chosen One
chapters.body: When the angels announced Isa to her, they announced something else first: 'O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds' (3:42). A young woman in the sanctuary of the House, dedicated to worship from childhood, guarding her chastity with such devotion that her guardian Zakariya found provision at her station out of season — 'this is from Allah' (3:37). When the command came, it came in the form of a visitor: a well-proportioned man. 'Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Compassionate from you, if you should be fearing Allah' (19:18). He answered: I am only the messenger of your Lord, to announce to you a pure boy (19:19). She asked how a son could come to one untouched by any man, and the reply stands over history: 'Your Lord says: it is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter decreed' (19:21).

chapters.heading: The Palm Tree and the Child Who Spoke
chapters.body: The labor came upon her beside the trunk of a date palm, and her pain drove her to say — the Qur'an preserves it gently — 'If only I had died before this and was a thing forgotten' (19:23). A voice called from below her feet: do not grieve; your Lord has provided a stream beneath you, and shake the trunk of the palm toward you; it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you; so eat and drink and be contented (19:24-26). Provision descended at the moment of her greatest vulnerability — water and dates, exactly what a laboring mother needs. Then the greater miracle: her people accused her of a monstrous thing, and the infant in the cradle spoke by Allah's permission — 'Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the scripture and made me a prophet, and He has made me blessed wherever I am' (19:30-31). Maryam's defense was her son's voice, and the Qur'an named its nineteenth surah for her — the only woman whose name titles a chapter, preserved for every generation of believers to recite until the end of time. Her son called her truthful, and Allah Himself said: 'and his mother was a supporter of truth' (5:75).

familyQuestion: Maryam was chosen 'above the women of the worlds.' What do you think made her so beloved to Allah — and what could you imitate starting today?

title: Asiya, Wife of Pharaoh
subtitle: The woman who defied the most feared tyrant on earth
sources: Qur'an 28:9 — 'a comfort for me and for you; do not kill him'
Qur'an 66:11 — her prayer from inside Pharaoh's house
Qur'an 28:8-9 — the infant Musa brought to her

chapters.heading: The Tyrant's House, Allah's Refuge
chapters.body: The most dangerous address in the world at that time was Pharaoh's palace — and that is exactly where Allah sent the newborn Musa. His mother placed him in the river; the river delivered him to the house of the man slaughtering every Israelite son; and the woman of that house, Asiya, took the baby into her arms and said the sentence that crossed an empire: 'a comfort for me and for you; do not kill him. Perhaps he may benefit us, or we may take him as a son' (28:9). Pharaoh's own court ran on fear, yet in its heart this woman protected the very child whose existence Pharaoh had ordered erased. While her husband built towers and called himself lord, Asiya believed in the Lord of the worlds in secret — the Qur'an will call what happened next her greatest moment.

chapters.heading: The Prayer Allah Kept Forever
chapters.body: When Pharaoh's cruelty pressed on her — and when her faith became known — she made the dua the Qur'an carved into Surah At-Tahrim as a model for every believer: 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people' (66:11). Look at the order of her prayer: nearness to Allah first, rescue second. Ibn Kathir and the classical commentators record that Pharaoh tortured her for her faith and that she died under it — and that as her suffering peaked, she saw her home in Paradise unveiled beside her, and smiled. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ named the great women of Paradise, and among them was the wife of Pharaoh (Sahih al-Bukhari 3411). A woman the world remembers only as 'Pharaoh's wife' — Allah remembers by her faith, and gave her what tyrants cannot touch.

familyQuestion: Asiya had everything a palace could offer and chose Allah instead. What would you hold onto if keeping it meant letting go of your faith?

title: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
subtitle: The first believer — the Prophet's ﷺ refuge and strength
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3 — the revelation and her response
Sahih al-Bukhari 3820 — the Prophet's ﷺ remembrance of her
Sahih Muslim 2432 — 'Allah will never disgrace you'

chapters.heading: The First 'I Believe You'
chapters.body: When the angel came to Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira and the weight of revelation began, he came home trembling and said: cover me, cover me. Khadijah held him and answered with the faith of a woman who had watched his character for fifteen years: 'Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with your kin, you help the weak, you honor the guest, you bear the hardship of the road, you help against the calamities of truth' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3). Then she took him to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who confirmed what had come to him. She was the very first human being to believe in the message — the one through whom Allah consoled His Messenger. Aisha said she never envied any of the Prophet's wives as she envied Khadijah, 'for he remembered her often' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3820).

chapters.heading: The Wealth That Became the Ummah's Seed
chapters.body: Khadijah was a merchant of Quraysh in her own right — a woman of independent wealth and impeccable standing who, the scholars record, had previously refused the marriage offers of the nobles of Makkah and chose Muhammad ﷺ. When the boycott came and the believers were starved in the valley, her wealth carried the community. The revelation descended in her lifetime at its most brutal, and the Prophet ﷺ lost her in the Year of Sorrow — the same year he lost his uncle Abu Talib. Aisha reported that whenever the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered a sheep he would say: send some to Khadijah's friends (Sahih al-Bukhari 3818). Decades after her death, the household still honored her people. The Mother of the Believers, the Mother of Fatima, the first soul to say la ilaha illa Allah beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

familyQuestion: Khadijah's trust came from years of watching the Prophet's ﷺ character. Whose character do you know so well that you would believe them in a moment of fear?

title: Aisha bint Abi Bakr
subtitle: The scholar of the Ummah — the Prophet's ﷺ beloved
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3742 — 'I was shown you in a dream'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2699 — the slander and her exoneration, Qur'an 24:11-26
Sahih al-Bukhari 3661 — the Prophet's ﷺ answer to her question about women

chapters.heading: The Girl Who Grew Up Beside Revelation
chapters.body: Aisha was raised inside the household of revelation itself — the daughter of Abu Bakr, married to the Prophet ﷺ while still young, and entrusted with what would become one of the greatest scholarly legacies in Islamic history. The Prophet ﷺ saw her in a dream before the marriage: twice he was shown a veiled figure and told, this is your wife — and when he uncovered her face it was Aisha, and the angel said: this is your wife (Sahih al-Bukhari 3742). Years later, when the hypocrites spread the slander against her, the household was shaken and revelation itself descended to clear her — an entire passage of the Qur'an, Surah An-Nur 24:11-26, descended in defense of one woman's honor (Sahih al-Bukhari 2699).

chapters.heading: The Teacher of a Generation
chapters.body: The scholars counted the hadiths she transmitted — over two thousand — and the great companions came to her with their hardest questions, because she had learned the deen in the first household of the deen. When she asked the Prophet ﷺ about women being described as deficient in intellect and religion, she pressed on — and he explained the matters plainly until she understood, not as a rebuke but as a teacher to a student he loved (Sahih al-Bukhari 304). The Prophet ﷺ was asked: which of your wives do you love most? He said: Aisha. Her father Abu Bakr stood in the mosque and said: if anyone asks, I am from the tribe of Taym — and her nephew Qutham said: I am from the tribe of Taym too, and the Prophet ﷺ smiled and said: as for you, you belong to me and my family (Sahih al-Bukhari 3499). She outlived him by decades and became the reference point of the early community — Umm al-Mu'minin, the Mother of the Believers, in truth and in fact.

familyQuestion: Aisha asked questions even when the answer was hard. When was the last time you asked a sincere question about your faith instead of pretending to understand?

title: Fatima al-Zahra
subtitle: The leader of the women of Paradise
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3623-3624 — the leader of the women of Paradise
Sahih al-Bukhari 3714 — 'You are a piece of me'
Qur'an 33:33 — the Verse of Purification (Ahl al-Bayt)
Sahih Muslim 2448 — her anger and the Prophet's ﷺ reconciliation

chapters.heading: A Piece of the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.body: Fatima was the youngest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and the one he called by a title he gave no other: when she came to him, he would rise for her, seat her in his place, and honor her — and when he visited her, she would rise and seat him (Sunan Abi Dawud 5217). To her he said: you are a piece of me (Sahih al-Bukhari 3714). The angel visited the Prophet ﷺ while Fatima, Ali, Hasan and Husayn were with him and recited over them: 'Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with purification' (33:33) — the Verse of Purity, Ahl al-Bayt (Sahih Muslim 2424). She carried the household through hunger, boycott, and loss — present at the death of her father, the grief of which, the historians say, never left her.

chapters.heading: The Inheritance of Dignity
chapters.body: When Fatima asked for a share of the Prophet's ﷺ estate after his passing, Abu Bakr answered her with his words: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: we are not inherited from; what we leave is charity' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3092) — and she accepted it. The scholars of seerah note that her brief disagreement with Abu Bakr was over this matter alone, and that the Prophet ﷺ had told her during his life what she would face — and taught her the words to say in the morning and evening that would suffice her against every harm (Sahih Muslim 2731). She lived months after her father, then followed him. Her legacy stood at Karbala and stands everywhere the household of the Prophet ﷺ is loved: Hasan and Husayn, the leaders of the youth of Paradise (Tirmidhi 3749). She is al-Zahra — the Radiant — and the Prophet ﷺ named her without hesitation: the leader of the women of Paradise (Sahih al-Bukhari 3624).

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ called Fatima 'a piece of me.' What does it mean to carry someone's honor so carefully that you protect it like your own body?

title: Hafsa bint Umar
subtitle: The keeper of the first Qur'an between two covers
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 4987-4988 — Abu Bakr gathers the leaves into one book
Sahih al-Bukhari 4680 — 'the most beloved of people to me after Abu Bakr was Umar'

chapters.heading: The Widow Who Became a Wife of the Prophet
chapters.body: Hafsa lost her husband in the battles of Badr and Uhud, and her father Umar — the second caliph — carried a father's worry for his widowed daughter. The Prophet ﷺ married her, joining the households of his two closest companions, and Umar's joy at the union is preserved in the books (Sahih al-Bukhari 4680). She was known for her worship and her firmness; a woman of the household of revelation, with the strength of her father and the sensitivity of her faith.

chapters.heading: The Leaves in Her Keeping
chapters.body: After the calamity of Yamamah, when many who had memorized the Qur'an were martyred, Umar came to Abu Bakr with his famous warning: the death of the reciters is death for the Book — gather it. Abu Bakr hesitated — how could he do what the Messenger ﷺ had not done? — and Umar pressed until the leaves and scraps, kept in the custody of Hafsa, were gathered into a single book (Sahih al-Bukhari 4987). When the copies were later standardized under Uthman, the master copy was the one kept with Hafsa — she returned it only on the promise that it would be returned (Sahih al-Bukhari 4988). Think of that: for a generation, the mother-text of the Qur'an lived with a woman, and the caliphate itself had to honor her terms. When Muslims anywhere in the world open a mushaf today, its lineage passes through her house.

familyQuestion: Hafsa held the most precious book on earth and treated it as a trust, not a possession. What has been trusted to you that you are responsible for protecting?

title: Zaynab bint Jahsh
subtitle: The first to follow the Prophet ﷺ from among the women
sources: Qur'an 33:37 — 'when Zayd had concluded his desire for her, We married her to you'
Qur'an 33:28-29 — her choice answered by Allah Himself
Sahih al-Bukhari 7420 — 'she who was the first to follow me'

chapters.heading: A Marriage Heaven Arranged
chapters.body: Zaynab was the Prophet's ﷺ cousin, and it was Allah who arranged her marriage to his freedman Zayd — a union meant to erase the Arab distinction between freeborn and freed. The Qur'an states it plainly: 'there is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has decreed for him' — and when Zayd ended the marriage, Allah completed what He had ordained: 'when Zayd had concluded his desire for her, We married her to you' (33:37). The chapter, Al-Ahzab, descended around the household of the Prophet ﷺ itself — no woman of that generation had her biography written into the revelation like Zaynab. What people might gossip about, Allah Himself narrated with honor.

chapters.heading: Generosity That Shook the Floor
chapters.body: Zaynab was famed across Madinah for two things: her needlework for the poor, and the sound of her giving. She tanned hides and sewed with her own hands, and her charity came so continuously that her floorboards creaked under it — the Prophet ﷺ called her and the women of the household together when a lean season arrived and said: which of you is the creaking-floor one? Zaynab kept silent. But when Allah offered the wives a choice — the glitter of this world, or Allah and His Messenger — Zaynab answered with the wives' famous words: we choose Allah and His Messenger (33:28-29), and Allah praised them in the Qur'an for it. In his final illness, the Prophet ﷺ visited her and smiled at her generosity, and she — the first of the women to follow him in death — rejoined him not long after he left this world (Sahih al-Bukhari 7420).

familyQuestion: Zaynab worked with her own hands for the poor. What skill do you have that could become someone's provision?

title: Umm Salama
subtitle: The woman whose question became a verse of the Qur'an
sources: Qur'an 3:152 — the day of Uhud, when some fled
Qur'an 33:35 — 'Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women...' revealed after her question
Musnad Ahmad 26674 — her famous words to the Prophet ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah

chapters.heading: The Wife Who Lost and Stayed
chapters.body: Umm Salama and her husband Abu Salama were among the earliest believers, and they bore the full weight of the early years: beaten for their faith, separated, and finally emigrating to Madinah. Then, in the campaign of Uhud, Abu Salama was fatally wounded — the verse of that day describes the believers struck while 'the one who turns back on that day, having been touched by evil, is as one driven by Satan' (3:152). A widow with small children, she heard the Prophet ﷺ teach the great words for the stricken: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with what is better' (Muslim 2123). She said them — and within a year the best of creation was at her door with a marriage proposal.

chapters.heading: One Question, One Verse
chapters.body: At the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ commanded the companions to slaughter and shave — three times — and no one moved, distressed at the terms of the treaty. He entered his tent and told Umm Salama what had happened, and she said the words of a strategist of faith: 'O Messenger of Allah, go out and do not speak to anyone until you have slaughtered your own animal and shaved your head. They will not refuse you.' He did exactly that, and the companions followed until not one remained (Musnad Ahmad 26674). And when she asked the Prophet ﷺ why the Qur'an spoke of the men but not the women, the answer was not a word to her alone — it was a verse of the Book for all time: 'Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women... Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward' (33:35; Tirmidhi 3050). A woman's question became a verse — ask, and the sky can answer.

familyQuestion: Umm Salama's question became part of the Qur'an. What question about your life or faith could you bring to Allah in prayer tonight?

title: Juwayriyya bint al-Harith
subtitle: The captive whose freedom unbound a hundred families
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 3927 — 'what became of your prisoner?' and the freeing of her people
Sahih Muslim 1365 — the day of the captives

chapters.heading: The Thirst and the Answer
chapters.body: After the battle against Banu al-Mustaliq, Juwayriyya, daughter of the tribe's chief, came to the Prophet ﷺ to seek help for her situation as a captive. The Prophet ﷺ offered to free her and marry her, and she accepted — a word that reached her people like rain on dry ground. When her father al-Harith came for her, he found her already honored in the household of the Prophet ﷺ, and he and his people embraced Islam together. The Prophet ﷺ then asked his companions: what became of your prisoner? — meaning her — and they said: we have freed her for what is owed to the Messenger of Allah. He replied: she is with you, meaning she had become their mother-in-faith, and the companions, ashamed to keep their captives now that the tribe was family, freed every captive of Banu al-Mustaliq — and the count of the freed, the scholars record, reached one hundred families or more (Sunan Abi Dawud 3927).

chapters.heading: A Captive Who Caught Barakah
chapters.body: Aisha described the day: Juwayriyya was a woman of such beauty and dignity that anyone who saw her loved her, and the hour the Prophet ﷺ freed her became an hour of freedom for her entire people. The believers who had taken captives returned them, saying: how can we hold the in-laws of the Messenger of Allah? One woman's marriage, one morning, and a hundred households walked free — a lesson the Prophet ﷺ embodied all his life: honor given returns multiplied, and the strongest hand is the one that opens. Aisha said she knew no woman more blessed for her people than Juwayriyya.

familyQuestion: One act of honor toward Juwayriyya freed a hundred families. What is one honorable act you could do this week whose ripple you may never fully see?

title: Umm Ayman (Barakah)
subtitle: The woman who raised the Prophet ﷺ — promised Paradise
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3835 — 'you still have some of my mother with you'
Sahih al-Bukhari 4076 — her presence at Uhud, shielding the wounded

chapters.heading: The Mother After the Mother
chapters.body: When Amina, the Prophet's ﷺ mother, died on the return from Madinah, the six-year-old boy came home to Makkah, and the household gave him into the care of Umm Ayman — Barakah, the Abyssinian servant who had served his parents and now served his childhood. She fed him, clothed him, and guarded him; when he grew and married Khadijah, she remained in his house as family, not staff. Years later, after the battles of Hunayn, when others came asking for gifts of the spoils, the Prophet ﷺ gave out camels to soften hearts — and to one man he gave a hundred camels. The young men said: you gave so-and-so a hundred and gave Umm Ayman only four? He answered with the honor that settles every argument: she still has some of my mother in her — meaning give her more (Tirmidhi 3835).

chapters.heading: At the Wounded on the Day of Uhud
chapters.body: On the day of Uhud, when the rumor spread that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed and the field broke, Umm Ayman was among the very few who moved toward the battle instead of away from it — tending the wounded, carrying water, and calling the fleeing men back with a courage that shamed them (Sahih al-Bukhari 4076). An old woman, unarmed, walking toward the spears. After the battle the Prophet ﷺ passed her and smiled at her, and she asked about her own son Ayman, who had been martyred that day — and the Prophet ﷺ told her that Ayman had been raised to the highest companionship. She answered with the patience that named her station: I am patient, and I hope for my reward from Allah. Zayd ibn Harithah, the Prophet's ﷺ adopted son, was her son too — and generations of believers who learned the meaning of 'some of my mother' learned it from her.

familyQuestion: Umm Ayman raised an orphan who became the best of creation. Who has cared for you when you had no one — and have you thanked them this year?
